description:
This archive supports the manuscript "Sharp Predictability Criteria and Waiting-Time Recovery Rates for Positive Hereditary Models". It provides loading-aware prediction-time computation code, frozen protocols, complete saved numerical outcomes and optimization witnesses, audits, figure-generation records and reproduction entry points. It is a research reproducibility release, not a claim of journal acceptance.

Version 1.1.0 is self-contained: baseline_v1.0.0/ retains every file of the preceding complete public archive, and review_evidence/ adds the complete prediction-time search, temporal transport, continuous-dual, matched strong-oracle and two measured-PVC studies. Distinct frozen source snapshots are preserved at their original relative paths. Only a manuscript-attachment layout QA receipt is excluded; no numerical case, negative result, fitting failure or solver witness is filtered out.

A matched synthetic strong-oracle comparison reduces endpoint programs from 1154 to 810 for 584 correlated requests, with a machine-specific median aggregate speed ratio of 1.359 and some slower tasks. A measured-PVC scheduling comparison uses 234 instead of 650 programs for 315 correlated requests, preserving final labels and first sufficient candidates; the original median ratio is 2.054. An earlier PVC sensitivity study retains one sufficient request out of 90 correlated requests on a different target list. These counts are not independent material trials or an improvement from one study's success count to the other.

The full failed orbital-fat pilot remains negative evidence. PVC error bands are assumed, and same-profile hold-state continuation does not validate cross-loading criteria or a positive waiting-time recovery exponent. Numerical replay does not establish calibrated material guarantees, population coverage, universal speedup, superior point-prediction accuracy or exclusive capability over classical optimization.

Original orbital-fat and PVC source files are attributed and retained unchanged under their source terms; derived analyses are identified separately. The authors' code is MIT-licensed, with separate third-party licence scopes in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. Do not treat the original source files as wholly MIT. The archive contains no editorial correspondence, author-only submission disclosures, manuscript PDF, virtual environment or third-party dependency source tree. It has a file-level SHA-256 manifest and a standard-library integrity verifier. No new physical measurements or scientific experiments are introduced by packaging.
